title: Planning public transport and safer streets: capacity, speed and Vision Zero
examples: Why does a bus lane carry more people than a car lane?
Why do 30 km/h limits save lives?

items.label: Bus lane
items.ask: Why do bus lanes move more people than car lanes?

explain.say: Each year about one point two million people die on the world's roads, according to the World Health Organization. Transport planners fight this, and traffic, with two tools: moving people instead of cars, and designing streets so mistakes are not deadly. First, look at how many people one lane can move in an hour.

draw.text: Planning public transport and safer streets: capacity, speed and Vision Zero

items.label: Bus lane
items.ask: Why do bus lanes move more people than car lanes?

explain.say: A car lane passes about eighteen hundred cars an hour, but with only about one point two people in each, that is roughly two thousand people. A bus lane with a hundred and twenty buses an hour, seventy five people each, moves nine thousand, over four times as many, in the same strip of road. Which lane would you give the most space in a crowded city?

items.label: Bus lane
items.ask: Why do bus lanes move more people than car lanes?

explain.say: The bus lane! Bus rapid transit goes further: its own lanes, stations where you pay before boarding, and level floors. Curitiba in Brazil pioneered it in 1974 and Bogotá's TransMilenio carries tens of thousands an hour on its busiest lines. Metros move even more. Planners place stops so most people live within a five to ten minute walk.

items.label: Bus lane
items.ask: Why do bus lanes move more people than car lanes?

explain.say: Now safety. Two cars see a child step out, one at thirty, one at fifty. Look at the graph. The slow car stops in seventeen and a half metres. At that very spot, the faster driver has not even started braking: still doing fifty! It needs almost thirty five metres. And crash energy grows with speed squared, so fifty carries almost three times the energy of thirty.

marks.label: Still at 50 km/h!
marks.ask: Why do 30 km/h speed limits save lives?

explain.say: That is the Safe System idea, born from Sweden's Vision Zero in 1997: people will make mistakes, so design roads where a mistake never costs a life, with low speeds where people walk. Superb work! Challenge: how many times more crash energy does a car at sixty carry than one at thirty?

faq.q: Why do bus lanes move more people than car lanes?
faq.a: Buses carry many people in little road space. A car lane moves about 2,000 people an hour, while a bus lane with 120 buses carrying 75 each moves about 9,000.
asks: Why does a bus lane carry more people than a car lane?

faq.a: BRT is a bus system with dedicated lanes, stations with off-board fare payment, level boarding and frequent service, giving metro-like speed at lower cost. Curitiba and Bogotá are famous examples.

faq.q: What is the Safe System approach?
faq.a: An approach to road safety that accepts people make mistakes and that the human body has limits, so roads, speeds and vehicles are designed so that crashes do not kill or seriously injure.

faq.q: Why do 30 km/h speed limits save lives?
faq.a: At 30 kilometres per hour a car stops in about half the distance needed at 50, and carries about a third of the crash energy, so many crashes are avoided and others are far less severe.
A road safety policy adopted by the Swedish parliament in 1997, with the goal that no one should be killed or seriously injured on the roads. Many cities worldwide now follow it.

facts: The WHO Global Status Report on Road Safety 2023 estimated about 1.19 million road deaths in 2021.
Sweden's parliament adopted Vision Zero in 1997.
Curitiba in Brazil opened its pioneering bus rapid transit system in 1974.
